description: Award loading... We are TheCosmicArchive, building innovative technology for the greater good of space exploration, currently building MarsNav the Google Maps/Survival Guide for Mars. Check it out in the Project tab! - Vihaan Prabhodh and Eric Laurent
summary:
MarsNav, a layered, interactive 3D map that helps astronauts plan and carry out a safe, science-focused Marswalk. It integrates NASA satellite imagery and terrain data into switchable layers showing slopes, rocks, minerals, cliffs, radiation zones, temperature, and wind, so explorers can see a route and its destinations in full detail.
To address the challenge, MarsNav combines data from multiple NASA missions into one view and adds real-time-style mission awareness. Its Safety System tracks radiation, temperature, wind and dust, suit oxygen, power, and radio communication, and checks whether a mission meets its safety requirements. Walk Stops guide astronauts to scientifically valuable sites, each with research objectives and estimated exploration times. Crew and Rover modes and simulations let teams test scenarios in advance. Everything is compiled into a downloadable Mission Report.
This matters because the first humans on Mars will be far from help, and every decision must be informed. MarsNav helps them complete missions quickly, safely, and with maximum scientific return.
details:
• Scientific Realism vs. Usability Grounded slopes, temperatures (-14 Celsius sunlit rock vs. -62 Celsius canyon shadow), dust opacity, radiation, and 20% suit reserve thresholds in published NASA datasets while keeping explanations in plain, human-readable language.
  • Crew Safety Margins Enforced buddy-pair route spacing, UHF radio line of sight checks, and direct emergency return-time calculations from the farthest waypoint back to Base Camp.
  • Accessibility & Field Ergonomics: Designed a high contrast dark volcanic UI (#0B0D10 / #EE5A1C), Glove Mode enlarged controls, keyboard-accessible interactive elevation scrubbing, and voice input/output.
  • Provenance & Transparency: Explicitly separated real NASA public domain orbital/rover imagery (PIA26306, PIA19303, PIA21606, PIA21041–21043, PIA25075) from simulated EVA prediction models inside a dedicated Resources & Provenance registry.
  • Performance: Kept 3D terrain rendering, stipple canvas textures, and multilayer map compositing lightweight so the full 3D planner runs smoothly in a standard browser.
